subject: Biotechnology
title: Genome Editing in Crops
description: A fast breakdown of Genome Editing in Crops for builders.

hook.text: CRISPR edits crop genes without adding foreign DNA — making changes indistinguishable from natural mutations.

buildup.text: CRISPR knocks out the gene that makes mushrooms brown — the non-browning mushroom was the first CRISPR crop.

discovery.text: USDA ruled that CRISPR crops with no foreign DNA are not regulated as GMOs — a game changer for small companies.

twist.text: Europe still regulates CRISPR crops as GMOs — identical edits face different rules on different continents.

climax.text: CRISPR tomatoes with higher GABA content launched in Japan in 2021 — the first gene-edited food sold to consumers.

punchline.text: Edit the crop's own genes — no foreign DNA, new traits, old debate.

quiz.question: Why did the USDA rule that some CRISPR crops are not GMOs?
options: CRISPR is too new to be regulated under existing laws
Edits without foreign DNA are indistinguishable from natural mutations
CRISPR crops have not been tested enough to require regulation
